title: Mixed-characteristic regular local pair models over a complete trait
statement:
Let $(B,\mathfrak m)$ be a complete strictly henselian Noetherian regular local ring of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$, of dimension $d\geq1$, with residue field $k$ [def-weil-regular-scheme, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology, def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring, def-weil-residue-field]. Mixed characteristic means that $B$ has characteristic zero and $k$ has characteristic $p>0$. Fix a prime $\ell$ invertible in $B$, and generators $t_1,\ldots,t_d$ of $\mathfrak m$ which form a regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. There exist a complete strictly henselian discrete valuation ring $C$ of mixed characteristic $(0,p)$ with residue field $k$ and $\ell$ invertible, a small nonempty directed set $I$, and a directed system of $C$-algebras $B_a$, with elements $t_{a,1},\ldots,t_{a,d}$ preserved by all transition maps, satisfying the following conditions. A discrete valuation ring here means a Noetherian local domain of dimension one with principal maximal ideal.

Each $B_a$ is a regular integral finitely generated $C$-algebra, is flat over $C$, and $t_{a,1},\ldots,t_{a,d}$ is a regular sequence. For $J_a=(t_{a,1},\ldots,t_{a,d})$, the quotient $B_a/J_a$ is regular Noetherian of characteristic $p$. There are compatible isomorphisms of rings
$$\varinjlim_a B_a\cong B,\qquad \varinjlim_a(B_a/J_a)\cong k,$$
under which the quotient maps induce $B\twoheadrightarrow k$ and $t_{a,r}$ maps to $t_r$.

In scheme language [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $V_a=\operatorname{Spec}B_a$ is integral regular, flat and of finite type over $S=\operatorname{Spec}C$ [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. It is quasi-projective over $S$: it admits a locally closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space over $S$. The regular closed subscheme $Z_a=\operatorname{Spec}(B_a/J_a)$ is cut out by the displayed equations, with constant codimension function $d$ in [def-per-regular-closed-immersion-codimension]. The limiting pair is $\operatorname{Spec}k\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}B$.

source.place: Agent-formulated simultaneous regular-pair approximation input for Expose XVI section 3.7, first paragraph, printed p.254; I Theorem 2.9 (Cohen), printed p.9; I Theorem 10.3(i) (Popescu), printed p.17; IV Theorem 4.1.8 (Cohen lifting), printed pp.56--57. Those ingredients do not state the entire simultaneous formulation verbatim. This is a fresh unsplit algebraic obligation.

proof.text: The displayed $d$ generators of $\mathfrak m$ are a regular system of parameters by [def-weil-pbc-regular-system-of-parameters]. Apply [lem-per-complete-mixed-regular-pair-approximation] to $R=B$, this ordered tuple, $p$ and $\ell$. Its completeness, strict henselianity, mixed characteristic, dimension and invertibility hypotheses are exactly those assumed here. Obtain $C$, $I$, and affine pairs $Z_a\hookrightarrow V_a$ with compatible marked regular sequences and limit $\operatorname{Spec}k\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}B$. The input also supplies quasi-projectivity of every $V_a$. The index is nonempty: if a convention permitted an empty directed set, its asserted limit $\operatorname{Spec}B$ would be terminal. By the morphism correspondence in [def-weil-affine-spectrum], $B$ would then be an initial commutative ring, hence isomorphic to $\mathbf Z$, which is not local (its distinct maximal ideals $(2)$ and $(3)$ contradict locality of $B$).

source.place: XVI 3.7, first paragraph, printed p.254; the complete-trait simultaneous-pair input is the existing node lem-per-complete-mixed-regular-pair-approximation. Parameter terminology: algebra.tex Tag 00KU (definition-regular-local).

proof.text: Put $B_a=\Gamma(V_a,\mathcal O_{V_a})$. The affine-spectrum morphism correspondence [def-weil-affine-spectrum] turns the structure maps and inverse transition maps into a directed system of $C$-algebras. Take $t_{a,r}$ to be the given marked global sections; their compatibility is unchanged. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-lft-affine-pairs] with the whole affine source $V_a$ and target $S$: the coordinate algebra $B_a$ is finitely generated over $C$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map-iff-flat-affine] to its structural homomorphism: $B_a$ is flat over $C$. The definition [def-pc-integral-scheme], applied to the nonempty affine open $V_a$ itself, says that $B_a$ is a domain.

source.place: Tags 01T2 (lemma-locally-finite-type-characterize), 01U5 (lemma-flat-characterize), with whole affine opens; properties.tex Tag 01OK (definition-integral).

proof.text: Write $J_a=(t_{a,1},\ldots,t_{a,d})$. By the affine closed-immersion description [def-weil-closed-immersion], the assertion that $Z_a$ is cut out by these equations identifies its coordinate ring with $B_a/J_a$, compatibly with inclusions and transitions. Regularity of $V_a$ and $Z_a$ gives local Noetherianity and regular local stalks by [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Apply [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth] to each whole affine scheme to obtain Noetherian coordinate rings. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], these stalks are precisely all prime localizations of the respective coordinate rings, so both rings are regular. The $\mathbf F_p$-scheme structure of $Z_a$ gives $p=0$ in $B_a/J_a$. This quotient is nonzero because the marked tuple is a regular sequence, by [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]; consequently its characteristic is exactly the prime $p$. The same marked tuple is regular on $B_a$, as supplied by the approximation input.

source.place: Tags 01OW (lemma-locally-Noetherian), 02IS/02IT (regular schemes); schemes.tex Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), morphisms.tex Tag 01QO (lemma-closed-immersion), algebra.tex Tag 00LF (definition-regular-sequence).

proof.text: The two ring colimits follow directly from the specified scheme limits and their universal properties. For any commutative ring $T$, a compatible family $B_a\to T$ corresponds by [def-weil-affine-spectrum] to a cone $\operatorname{Spec}T\to V_a$. The limit assertion of [lem-per-complete-mixed-regular-pair-approximation] gives a unique $\operatorname{Spec}T\to\operatorname{Spec}B$, hence a unique $B\to T$ inducing the given family. This is exactly the colimit property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit], so $\varinjlim B_a\cong B$ with the prescribed coprojections. Apply the identical argument to $B_a/J_a$ and $Z_a$ to get $\varinjlim(B_a/J_a)\cong k$. The limiting inclusion in that input is the specified residue inclusion, so its ring map is $B\twoheadrightarrow k$, and compatibility of the marked equations says exactly that $t_{a,r}$ maps to $t_r$. Thus these are compatible isomorphisms of the displayed quotient diagrams.

source.place: Affine-spectrum morphism correspondence, Tag 01I1 (lemma-morphism-into-affine); categories.tex Tag 002F (definition-colimit). The argument is the universal property, applied to the limits already given by the approximation input.

proof.text: Keep the schemes $V_a$ and $Z_a$ from the input, under the affine identifications above; their flatness, integrality, regularity, finite type and quasi-projectivity have already been supplied or identified. For every $z\in Z_a$, choose the whole affine $V_a$ in [def-per-regular-closed-immersion-codimension]. Its kernel is $J_a$ and the displayed regular sequence has length $d$; therefore its codimension function in that definition is the constant function $z\mapsto d$. The compatible limits remain the pair $\operatorname{Spec}k\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}B$ specified by the input. This verifies the scheme-language clauses with exactly the same equations and quotient maps.
